Due to the simple nature of preacher curl benches I just can’t justify paying over $100 for one. That being said, when you value shop sometimes you regret not going for the higher priced item. Not so in this case. While it may not have the thickest padding or thickness of steel as a more expensive bench, I am confident it will serve me well. The elbow pad has sufficient pad thickness and is not uncomfortable. Some reviews have stated that the pad needs to be wider. I don’t disagree that it would be nice if they were, and it might be necessary for a large framed person. My husband is 5'9" and broad in the shoulders. I am 5'4" and its perfect for me. For close grip curls there is no issue, but wide grip you are toward the edge. In my husband's case, it didn't affect his workout. Everything works as it should and feels sufficient and sturdy. It only took ten minutes to put together and I was good to go. For me this was a good value to suit my needs and I am pleased with my purchase. As long as you are realistic about what you can obtain for the price you will not be disappointed. I do recommend this bench and will keep my eye on this brand for future items.

TISUR Titanium Key Rings for Keychains, Quick Release Side Pushing Key Organizer Kit, Wisely Group Your Keys I like the way these rings work - you don't have to use fingernails or overcome a lot of tension to open the ring, and using them doesn't scratch them up or wear off the finish and create shiny spots. They seem resistant to being bent out of shape too...and all while being pleasantly lightweight. They're just...Keyring 2.0. A far superior alternative to the keyring model we've been struggling with for decades now.

Update: Yes, being titanium, they are indeed resistant to being bent out of shape. We have a little devil dog who likes to destroy things; I think it gives him a sense of agency. :) And one of the things he discovered he likes to do is pull the tags off his and his sister-dog's collars. The thin wire rings we originally used to attach the tags to collars made this easy for our destroyer-dog - he just pulled, and the wire rings would bend to allow him to pull the tags right off. I replaced those wire rings with TISUR titanium ones; they're nice and lightweight for the doggles' comfort, and our mechanically-inclined beast hasn't managed to pull a tag off either collar since.

I never thought there could be so much to say about something so simple as a keyring, but these really are next-level - an evolutionary stage beyond the classic keyring we've all used since I was a kid. Highly recommended for strength, light weight, and ease-of-use, all of which surpass the old design by a long shot.

There is the top compartment which is small but will fit mace, or other small items you might need on your ride.

STRAPS
The straps are really comfortable, not at all binding and are perfect for riding. There are a few spots to put some small items on through loops if you need to. There is a front strap that holds them together too. Again perfect.

WATER DISPENSING
This holds a great amount of water. Despite being heavy, this is very well centered. The water dispensing tube has a double system. First you flip the lever to seal it and lock it shut, then you have the silicone closure which you have to kind of press open with your teeth and suck on with your mouth. The water comes out very easily.

MAGNETIC CLOSURE
The magnetic closure on this hydrating pack is slid out while you ride to free up the tube, and then when you put it back, the magnet pulls it into place so it is easy to use while riding.

ANY PROBLEMS OR LEAKING?
There were no instructions with this and the lever that is flipped is a pain to use while riding. I have tried it with the lever in an open position and so far not leaking, but I am not sure how long that will last.

BACK PADDING
This is fabulous. It has a tunnel in it which allows for the back to stay cooler. It really does provide some nice airflow.

COMFORT
This is VERY comfortable to wear. It is almost as if it is not on, it is so well centered on the back.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This hydration pack is fantastic. It is easy to wear and use (once the lever is opened), has a nice magnet to keep it in place, and is centered beautifully with great airflow to the back.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This does not have tons of storage room on it, but enough for essentials. It is a very handy item and we have used it a lot so far and will continue to do so. HIGHLY recommended.
text_fidelity_b: CamelBak Skyline LR 10 Bike Hydration Backpack - Crux Lumbar Reservoir - 100 oz

text_fidelity_a:
SPRI Stash It Belt One of the most frustrating things for me is if I want to go for a long walk in a rural area and I have to have a phone near by. I prefer to walk without a phone and such, but at times I can not escape the need to have a phone for an important phone call. I really don't like a fanny pack, as it is really big, but was looking for something handier.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This stash belt is very thin. It is deceiving, however. The belt itself is a good quality stretchy elastic. It is heavy duty but not so heavy that it is bulky. There is a black clip in the back, and a slide to make the belt longer or shorter. The pack itself is 2 inches by 9 inches. However, it has a pleat in the top and bottom which make it bigger.

There is a water resistant lining in the pack, a front zipper, and a very thin reflective strip on the front. At full length, the belt measures 34 inches unstretched, and 41 inches stretched. The shortest is 24 inches stretching to about 32 inches.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
When using this, I can put my smart phone into the pack, a set of keys and a few cards. I can also stick in a tissue or two folded small. A huge set of keys will make it a bit tight, but a reasonable ring of keys with several keys on it should be fine. The pack does stretch a little bit so that things will fit.

As far as use, I found that this is very handy. I have to stretch it a little tight so that it does not bobble around as I walk. That is okay though, because it holds it in place. Otherwise, the phone and things can make it sag a little bit. Finding the right tightness takes a bit of trial and error. I really appreciate having this as it makes it the closet to walking without anything that I have been able to get.

THE BOTTOM LINE
I really like this stash belt. It is handy, useful, and makes it so that I can go for long walks without bulky bags or packs. Safe and with decent capacity, I can carry what I want to have with me yet feel free and lightweight at the same time. With a range of sizes it will fit, many people would benefit from this, but if you are a big and tall man, it might be a bit tight.

RATING
Five stars for this. I really like it. It is handy and easy to use. I will update if I have anything else important to add in the future.
text_fidelity_b: SPRI Stash It Belt

text_fidelity_a:
Horizon Fitness EX-59 Elliptical Trainer I would actually give this a 4.5 likely. One thing that bothers me is that it's light enough that when I stand with my feet at the back of the treads and don't step too lightly, the front end lifts up a little bit. I just adjust my stride.
It's QUITE quiet. The only real noise is the friction of the runners at the base, unavoidable. Watching TV or listening to music easily drowns it out. The beeps mentioned by others IS also annoying. It's loud for no good reason. After the warranty is up, I might look into opening it up and putting something to adjust the level. I ran for a little over an hour today with my wife sitting only ~6 feet away watching TV and it didn't bother her at all.

I'm 5'9" and the height is fine. My setup isn't - best place to use is under a build (down) ceiling covering heating ducts, so it's pretty low. If I'm not careful, I bump my forehead. The fan blows more on my chest than neck or face.

I'm currently not in the greatest shape, but I generally use it at the 4th or 5th intensity level and move at the 6.8 (mph?) pace. I've used it 4 times for a total of about 4:30 hrs. My shoes were tight, so once I took them off. Bad idea. The treads were not good on my feet; the soles are still sore.

It fits in a small space much better than I expected. It can easily set almost right up next to a wall, unless you need access from either side.

I don't imagine I'll test out the speakers much, as if I'm running inside, I'll likely watch TV shows or movies, or do as I do when I run outdoors, listen to music with earbuds.

After a couple uses I noticed that I could hear a jingling sound. I remembered to check it after today's session and the bolt/nut on the front right tread was loosening. Glad I caught it. I tightened it up and will keep an eye on it.

So far I'm quite happy with choosing this elliptical. If I had the extra $200, I might have gone with the next model up, but I have no regrets on this purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Horizon Fitness EX-59 Elliptical Trainer

text_fidelity_a:
Sportline 885 Flip Pack Hydration Waist Pack I had to submit my review after reading the other ones that didn't rate it so high. I have not had the same issues with my pack. It's exactly what I've been looking for. I've been running for two years and had previously used a standard pack that has one water bottle that sat right in the small of my back. However, I had been looking for away to attach my iPhone to it safely since I couldn't stand using an arm band.

I was so excited when I saw this pack in the store. It was just what I had been wanting. However, although it has the perfect holder for an iPhone, I was a little reluctant to purchase this at first because I was 1.) worried that it would be awkward running with a pack in the front; 2.) worried that the velcro would not be enough to keep the phone velcroed down and from flopping around....also the normal wear and tear on the velcro from flipping up the phone to note my pace on my RunKeeper app.

Admittedly, the pack doesn't work so well in the direct front as a runner...would probably be okay for a walker. However, there is too much bounce to allow that to be comfortable. It did much better when I moved it around to the back...however, it defeated the purpose of being able to monitor my pace as I was running.

I finally figured out that if I put it on my right side with the bottle toward the back part, that I could accomplish everything I needed. iPhone and app are easily accessible..in fact, I rarely need to flip up the phone to see my pace. I can usually see it by barely tipping it up. The water bottle is still handy and I'm able to use my arms without smacking it.

So, while I'm not strictly using it as designed, it suits my purpose just like I needed. I'm really happy with it. Some other things:

1.) The belt isn't that big. If your waist size is 40 inches plus, you might have a tough time getting it to snap.
2.) The water bottle holder is great. My old holder was all material. I like the reinforced strips that make it stiff enough to jam the bottle back in...yet is lightweight and holds the bottle tightly.
3. Water bottle is pretty standard...just right.
4.) The zippered pouch is bigger than I orginally thought. Holds spare key, chapstick, Gu and $ just fine.
text_fidelity_b: Sportline 885 Flip Pack Hydration Waist Pack

Keystand Kids Snorkel Mask Full Face, Breathing Mechanism Snorkeling Masks, Flat Crystal Lens, 180° Panoramic Anti-Leak/Anti-Fog Mask and Snorkel with Detachable Camera Mount I've used a mask and snorkel for fun, for at least the last 50 years, and spent over 20 years as a professional scuba diver, as part of my job. I've always used a traditional mask for snorkeling and diving, and have had my share of leaky seals, fogged glass, broken hardware, and mouthfuls of salty water. This new generation of full-face masks with an integrated snorkel really does represent a breakthrough, in several respects.

I was intrigued when I first saw integrated full-face snorkel masks like this one a few years ago, and have finally decided to give one a try. I'm glad that I did.

There are many design features that really do make this snorkel mask a game changer for me. I particularly like the separate, sealed compartments that separate your eyes/cheeks/forehead from your nose and mouth. This minimizes fogging that can be caused by inadvertently breathing into a traditional mask through your nose, making it hard to see in the water. It also keeps any water that leaks in around your chin away from the glass that you see through. That's important to me, because I have a beard that does sometimes let water leak into my mask.

The seal on this mask is a soft, doubled-over flap that does an admirable job. I have a thin face and it is often difficult to find a mask that seals well. This one does. And it does a surprisingly good job sealing over my beard, which I try to keep short.

The air comes in through the top of the mask, and travels through one-way valves to the lower chamber where your mouth and nose are. Exhalations exit through purge valves near your jaw. This system works well, but I wish that the air opening at the top of the mask, where the snorkel enters, was larger. It sometimes feels like I have to work too hard to get a big breath of air, which can lead to a feeling of claustrophobia and, for some users, I expect, panic. A bigger airway would probably alleviate this.

There is a place to install a go-pro style action camera, which I will be using for sure. It's a thoughtful addition that will simplify saving and sharing my adventures.

The snorkel has a float valve that keeps water from flooding the mask when you dive. This sort of valve is great for playing near the surface, but probably not reliable for deep diving.

You can't use this mask for scuba diving, because there's no way to get your regulator into your mouth. For regular snorkeling though, I have a new favorite mask!
text_fidelity_b: Keystand Kids Snorkel Mask Full Face, Breathing Mechanism Snorkeling Masks, Flat Crystal Lens, 180° Panoramic Anti-Leak/Anti-Fog Mask and Snorkel with Detachable Camera Mount

The rear switch is perfect for carrying the light in your fist and working with your thumb. A real plus: it has flat sides so when you put it down it does not roll away!

The light itself is very bright (I almost want to advise "Do not look into light with remaining eyeball"), especially on the highest setting. You can adjust the aperture for a wide or a narrow beam. text_fidelity_a:
Biscuits & Gravy | Freeze Dried Backpacking & Camping Food |2 Servings I was really surprised at how well they hit the exact flavor and consistency that I love from biscuits and gravy with this meal! This was my first mountain house dehydrated meal that I have ever eaten, and I learned a lot from testing it out. I actually picked up a few flavors in the last couple weeks just to taste them and know which ones I would actually like to bring backpacking or keep in my emergency supply kit.

What I learned from this is that I need to make sure that my water is seriously boiling hot and not just boiled five minutes ago. I also need to measure extremely carefully and definitely not short it on water. And also I need to not worry about the meal getting soggy, and instead taste a bite, and close the packet again and let it soak in some more if that is not fully rehydrated.

Overall, this was a perfect introduction to how fresh and delicious food like this can taste. We actually had some garden zucchini to eat on the side, and so having the biscuits and gravy, a fried egg, and some garden zucchini, all able to be cooked up on the camping stove, was amazing! It felt like a full, amazing meal, and even if I didn't have the egg or zucchini available, I would've been very happy to eat this.

In addition, there are some types of wheat that really bother me, and I wanted to find out if the wheat used in this product gave me that specific allergic reaction that I get to so many, even high quality, foods. I was absolutely delighted to find out that I did not experience any of the itching, swollen eyes, or other sensations that I occasionally get from eating wheat from certain brands. I am now feeling more confident to test out different flavors from this brand and definitely will include this specific flavor in my camping and emergency supply box. The portion size was enough to feed both myself, and my four and six-year-old kids, with accessory foods on the side to fill out the meal.
text_fidelity_b: Biscuits & Gravy | Freeze Dried Backpacking & Camping Food |2 Servings

Where things get a bit more premium and specialized are the Kip Leather baseball gloves. These can be found in both USA Kip Leather and Japanese Kip Leather. Kip leather is usually the most preferred leather among professional players due to the light, firm, feel and higher quality of the leather. Kip leather comes from younger cattle, which creates a lighter hide that is extremely durable and taut, while also being a little bit easier to break in when compared to USA premium steerhide gloves.

Selecting Your Leather:

Cowhide Leather - Heavy leather, fastest break in time, medium quality, short durability, ideal for youth players.

Steerhide Leather - Heaviest leather, longest break in time, high quality, longest durability, ideal for high school and college players.

Kip Leather - Lighter leather, medium break in time, higher quality, long durability, ideal for college and pro players.

Japanese Kip Leather - Lightest leather, medium break in time, highest quality, long durability, ideal for elite pro players.

text_fidelity_a:
Spec-Ops Brand Better BDU Belt 1.5-Inch I needed a BDU belt that would effectively fit my cargo shorts and hold up my IWB holster while carrying a Springfield .45 Mod 2. After researching various belts it became obvious that I needed a 1.5" wide belt to fit my belt loops, it had to be flexible enough to be comfortable around my surgically repaired abdomen, and it had to be strong enough to hold my Mod 2 in the right position for an effective draw. Since Florida is a concealed carry state, although they are currently considering open carry, my rig has to avoid printing so that it doesn't point out that I have a CCW in my possession. No sense in attracting unwanted attention from the public and law enforcement.

Over the years I have slowly moved up from carrying a NAA .22 magnum to a Kahr 9mm. The NAA .22 magnum is easily carried in any pocket with no printing issues. Stepping up to the Kahr 9mm was as easy as using a Sticky Holster inside my right front pocket. But carrying a far heavier and bulkier .45 took a little planning and trial and error. The clothing and belt have to be right, the carry position simple to access, and the weapon has to be concealed from public view.

I have the correct combination now thanks to this Spec-Ops BDU belt. It fits my regular belt loops, fastens securely around my waist, holds the weapon and holster in the proper position, is very comfortable, and instills the confidence needed when carrying a heavier weapon. I highly recommend this belt as a cost effective solution to carrying bulkier weapons.

As another interesting observation, each belt comes with a one page instruction sheet with illustrations. I have received many different products where an instruction manual/sheet would be very useful, and of course didn't get one. Spec-Ops wants to make sure that you get to use all the benefits of these belts. Smart!

Note: I like this belt so much that I now have it in three colors. Made in America no less!
text_fidelity_b: Spec-Ops Brand Better BDU Belt 1.5-Inch

Kryptonite New York 1210 Bike Chain Lock, 3.25 Feet Long Heavy Duty Anti-Theft Sold Secure Gold Bicycle Chain Lock with Evolution Disc Lock and Keys for Ultimate Security E-Bike, Motorcycle, Scooter I own a chain just like this. See my review here: [[ASIN:B000AMVPUM Kryptonite New York Chain 3' With Key Lock]]

The problem with these giant chains is a sense of added security, but I'm not convinced you get it with something like this. Big bolt cutters will demolish this thing (for evidence, search youtube for "security chains vs. bolt choppers", skip to 6min24s... this chain gets demolished in less than a minute. Granted, they're huge bolt cutters. But someone running around in a van at 3AM isn't going to care.). Couple the questionable security with how big of a pain this thing is to lug around (I've owned the chain for years) and I can't imagine it's worth it.

Anyway, since no bike lock seems to be impervious to bike theft, it's important for people to realize the only true security is to store the bike within sight (your home, place of work, near you on a restaurant patio, etc.). I imagine the latest and greatest u-locks are a better option due to the shear time it takes to grind through them (with bolt cutters not being an option), but I'd wager all bike chains are susceptible to big bolt cutters.

ORRSTAR 8-Person Tent for Camping Waterproof Windproof Family Tent with Top Rainfly Camping Tents Big and Large We have company coming this summer. This involves a few tents, but one of the people needs an inflatable mattress and room for stuff. This tent is who we got this for.

ASSEMBLY
Assembly was not difficult in our trial run. The instructions were pretty easy to follow and it does not take more than a half hour to put up with two people unless you are with someone VERY efficient in putting up tents.

WITHOUT FLY
Without the fly, this is a very nice tent - bright, airy, and lots of upper mesh to see the sky. This is perfect on nice days.

WITH FLY
The days that rain might be expected are the challenge. The fly is dark blue. The dark blue makes this tent feel very warm and almost oppressive some days, but it does protect in the rain. My point is if you are the type who does not want to take the fly off and put it on constantly, this might be a big dark for you to leave on constantly, unless you plan to just sleep inside and don't care.

STAKES
The stakes that come with this are not big enough to support the weight of wind and other frustrations. We got spiral stakes to use with this at least on the key points of stress and it works better.

STURDY?
We are only using this for this summer, so hopefully it will last through several weeks of use. We have not had any high winds or severe storms yet so I will have to update as to how well this worked for that.

STORM PROOFING
One thing we learned about tents over long term is that double tarps are a good idea. We put one down under the tent leaving a perimeter that is not too big around the edge. Then we put another inside the tent to further protect should there be a deluge.

STORAGE
I find that having a separate nylon bag for the fly helps a lot when it comes time to put this tent away. It allows for a faster pick up time and less frustrating trying to make everything fit.

SIZE
This is perfect for a queen sized mattress, 1 or 2 people and their stuff.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is great for a family with sleeping bags and not much stuff, or for less people and more stuff. The stakes could be better, the storage bag bigger, and perhaps a bit tougher construction/fabric, but all in all this is a decent tent and serves our purpose well- I hope.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS at this point. I will update once summer is over as to the longevity of this tent over several weeks.
text_fidelity_b: ORRSTAR 8-Person Tent for Camping Waterproof Windproof Family Tent with Top Rainfly Camping Tents Big and Large

text_fidelity_a:
Kuat Dirtbag This mount was exactly what I needed. I had built a fork mount roof rack for my fatbike out of an old Thule rack. I originally used a sunlite fatbike fork mount, but after the nut fell off that mount and not being able to buy a new one, I had to replace the whole unit.
I bought the 135mm X 9mm fork mount. This fits fatbike forks with 135mm spacing with quick release. I have. 2014 Specialized fatboy and it fits perfect. It won't fit through axle forks like the Bluto which are 150mm X 15mm. This mount does not come with a 135mm skewer, so you can either buy an extra, or use the one from your wheel. The rear wheels of most mountain bikes is 135mm so they are pretty common and affordable. The fork rests on two short metal tubes the same size as your axle, and just like your axle the skewer goes through the metal tubes to anchor your fork to the mount. This design is ingenious. There has been mention of misalignment in other reviews, mine did not have that problem. If the skewer falls off or someone steals it, you only have to replace the skewer and not the whole unit. This mount is good quality and should last awhile.
text_fidelity_b: Kuat Dirtbag

I took my time because some reviews cited the mount as a weak link as well as disputing whether or not this is the 'brightest'. I will admit that the mount seems flimsy, but in six weeks of relatively hard use it has held up.

As for brightness, I cannot say that it is or isn't the brightest. I will say that it illuminates a narrow path in front of you and definitely is oncoming driver friendly.

One thing about the mount is it will snap the light in place and firmly hold it if you follow the instruction sheet. It also quick releases the light so it will not get stolen when you chain your bike and go shopping or whatever. Plus it, like the tail light, installs without tools. I love that feature. I also love the fact that this light charges using a standard USB cable and not some proprietary one with a barrel connector. That is one of the reasons why I awarded this five stars.

Since the product specs cover the use and charging times in depth, I will not recite them here. I will say that I run mine at 100% brightness all the time and the 1.5 hour use time is fairly accurate.

There may be better lights on the market, but not at this one's price. I am thoroughly pleased with it and happy that I gave it six weeks before rushing to review it. In my opinion there is nothing seriously wrong with it and a lot that is right.

text_fidelity_a:
A SLICE RED Packable Backpack Small Waterproof Travel Hiking Daypack I gave the A SLICE RED Ultra Lightweight Packable Backpack (In black) 5 stars as you can see.

Here is my situation. I hunt. Don't find much but I hunt a lot and I have this big professional camo honkering GREAT backpack. I could survive everything but a nuclear war with only that thing. And that's a good thing...but...

I also often hunt out of a portable tree stand and that big old pro back unit is just a mess in that situation. Clunky, And it's heavy! So I was really looking forward to my new backpack for the purpose. I moved the essentials from my pro pack to the new one and it's exactly what I was looking for.

The A SLICE RED Ultra Lightweight Packable Backpack is a baby backpack for sure. It's a dufflebag put together in the shape of a backpack actually. When you get it stuffed it becomes the backpack. It has a front pocket. A mesh side pocket, good for a bottle of water or necessary paper..whatever you like. And the interior, at least for my purposes is plenty roomy. I have room to spare. That surprised me. Unlike the big boys this little pack adds zero weight to whatever you put in there. That's a bonus. The zippers worked fine, btw. Backstraps are adjustable. A little flimsy compared to high dollar, but they don't slip

Is it rough and tumble? Probably not. I wouldn't trust it in rough country with briars and such...but for normal use, it's fine. It is a day hiker or a day hunter. From the cost point and utility it's a fine choice for normal wear. I'm very pleased.

Gaiam Yoga Mat - Folding Travel Fitness & Exercise Mat - Foldable Yoga Mat for All Types of Yoga, Pilates & Floor Workouts (68"L x 24"W x 2mm Thick) I admit, I have a minor addiction to yoga mats! As an avid yogi and a newly certified yoga instructor, I think it never hurts to have a spare mat around--especially a handy foldable travel one.

This mat arrived folded, not rolled like most mats. I have an older travel mat (which I believe was also made by Gaiam), and although that one could be folded as well, it didn't have the same perforated-like grooves as this one which make folding easier. I actually really liked these grooves--not only did they help the mat to both fold flat AND lie flat, but also I found that they assisted with alignment of my hands and feet. I was also pleasantly surprised to see that this mat is just as wide as the full-size mat that I use for my regular home practice (see below), as somehow, it appeared smaller. Of course, this could also be considered a slight negative--i.e., although the mat does fold flat, it would still take up the space of a large book/binder when traveling.

This mat is quite thin, just 2mm. That may be a problem for some; it wasn't for me. My preferred mat for home practice is the [[ASIN:B009LHXD3O Manduka EKO Lite]], which is 4mm, so I am used to a thinner mat. I found that the grip or "stickiness" of the mat was pretty good--very good for standing poses, but my hands did slide a teeny bit in downward-facing dog. (My old travel mat actually performed a bit better in this regard.) Another minor issue was that the mat slide around somewhat on the floor; I have never had this problem with my other, heavier mats.

Certainly I would not recommend this mat for everyday use. As a travel mat, however, this Gaiam Foldable Yoga Mat should perform quite well for most.
text_fidelity_b: Gaiam Yoga Mat - Folding Travel Fitness & Exercise Mat - Foldable Yoga Mat for All Types of Yoga, Pilates & Floor Workouts (68"L x 24"W x 2mm Thick)

text_fidelity_a:
TFO Air Camping Sleeping Pad 1lb Ultralight, Upgraded 40D Tear-Resistant Nylon, Textured Inflatable Camping Mat with Compact Carrying Bag for Backpacking/Hiking The Earth is the world's largest heat sink & everyone who has slept on the ground knows that the earth will suck all the heat from your body as you try to sleep. This mat rolls up very compact, fills quickly & breaks down quickly. It is superior in every way to the pool float a lot of people (myself included) use.

This mat uses dozens of little chambers instead one big one which makes it fill faster & breaks down easier. The fill valve does not have a protrusion like a straw or a nipple, rather I kind of had to "kiss" it to blow it up. I was able to blow it up in about 65 seconds (I timed it). The port has a check valve that works very well so the air stays inside the mattress. The valve flaps around a bit & makes a squeaking sound that my wife compared to a Wookie.

To deflate, the valve opens to a 1" diameter hole. Because of the multiple air chambers, air does not get trapped in the rolled end when rolling it up. This makes a huge difference because it can be folded before all of the air is out. It took me 2 minutes to deflate, roll & bag the mat. Of course this is in my living room & not in 2-person tent.

I confess that I haven't slept on this mat yet but I did lay & roll around on it. It is just as noisy as my Thermarest mat and feels about the same thickness. It's not uncomfortable but also not particularly supple. It is on par for this type of low-profile, inflatable mat.

I usually tent-camp off my motorcycle where weight isn't so important but space is. This mat is way more compact than any of my other mats. If I was tent camping from the car I would probably stick with my self-inflating mat but this will definitely go on my next motorcycle trip. It is very light, probably light enough for hiking or biking but I can't speak to that.
text_fidelity_b: TFO Air Camping Sleeping Pad 1lb Ultralight, Upgraded 40D Tear-Resistant Nylon, Textured Inflatable Camping Mat with Compact Carrying Bag for Backpacking/Hiking

SWIFT - 199$
- Tiny Field of View
- Walking is barely possible on a street with no obstacles, but not recommended
- Viewing Distance is no further than your backyard
- You will be visible at night with it’s Red eyes when IR is On
- Comes with a convenient and good quality hard case to keep your device safe

RED - 299$
- Massive improvement in Field of View
- Display seems slightly blurry but in general better quality (Less Noise)
- Viewing Distance is the same
- Great improvement with the Camo for the IR eyes - You will not be as visible at night even on full IR setting
- Does NOT come with a hard case - which is a shame
- Supports Video and Photo recording with Audio (1080p)

In conclusion, if you are considering cheap night vision, you may just skip the SWIFT and take a look at the RED HD
They are both mildly useful but more of a toy

Very balanced to sit in, doesn't feel like you'll fall at all. Sure, it's a couple pounds, but when you get to camp and your friends are all sitting on a cold, wet log trying to find the good spot around the fire, you'll be lounging in comfort.

text_fidelity_a:
Sunny Health & Fitness Folding Incline Treadmill I've owned several lower end treadmills over the past 20+ years, but the T-4400 is my first Sunny, and it's the best of the under-$500 treadmills I've owned. The description and videos are accurate; I chose it partly because I wanted a treadmill that offered a no-incline option and an incline option and some kind of shock absorption, and this has both. And it's worth mentioning that the treadmill was very well packaged to avoid damage in shipping.

Since I walk or speed walk on treadmills, the first and to me most important thing about the Sunny Health & Fitness Folding Treadmill T4400 is that doesn't slow down or bog down when I'm walking on it. The other treadmills I've owned dragged when you walked - they'd slow down and speed up, and you can hear their motors struggling. Every one was properly oiled before use, and the tension was correct, so I guess they had weaker motor or the motors had less torque. The Sunny doesn't have this issue, and we did oil it first as per instructions.

I like the way it opens slowly so I don't have to do something keep it from slamming to the floor, potentially damaging the floor or the treadmill. A big surprise is that the heart rate monitor on mine is accurate - I tested it wearing a pulse oximeter while holding the heart rate monitor at the same time, and they both read the exact same number. I like the speed up and slow down buttons on the arms, but I did hit the speed up button a couple times when I meant to slow down.

Some people complain that the arms are too low. Well, I'm only 5' 3 1/2, and they were comfortable for me. They could be low for taller people, but I found them just right.

One thing that is probably not going to be accurate for most people is the calorie count. Unlike most machines that overcount, this under-counts the calories dramatically for me. That's okay - I have apps and a heart rate monitor. I have no idea if the distance calculated is correct, but for me, that's not an issue.

Instead of a treadmill mat, we put pieces of dense ethylene vinyl acetate foam sheets - fairly thick sheets - under each foot, and it made the treadmill quieter and reduced the impact of walking on it just a little.

Two last things. First, I've owned other Sunny products, and I also called them with questions about this treadmill. Both their phone and email support have been friendly and helpful. Also my husband bought this for me with his Amazon account, which is why it's not showing as a verified purchase.

I wasn't expecting much out of this Sunny Health & Fitness T4400, which is why I am so impressed. Many treadmills claim to have 0% incline, but in reality they have an incline - the Sunny is 0% or so close that I can't tell, and for someone in average condition, the higher incline is helpful. The heart rate monitor is accurate, the motor doesn't bog down when walking fast, slow, with or without an incline, and the display is easy to read. The shock absorbers aren't as good as a Sole, but for less than a quarter of the price, they do help and you can put a rubber mat under it to absorb a bit more impact. I'm so happy with this that when it comes time to upgrade, I'll most likely get another Sunny.
text_fidelity_b: Sunny Health & Fitness Folding Incline Treadmill

text_fidelity_a:
Sig Sauer BUCKMASTERS Scope- 3-12x44MM BDC It's been a while now, but products coming out of China are starting to rival top quality manufacturing elsewhere. This scope is a clear sign of that. The coating is smooth with no blemishes, the glass is properly and evenly multi-coated, the reticle is straight, and knobs give you decent feedback on the turns, and the flaps have tastefully relieved SIG logo on the inside (so when you flip them open EVERYONE can see what you working with [as if it matters] but still cool). The throw lever had some blemishes on it and wasn’t screwed all the way in. The Box it comes in is very simplistic – a good thing – with minimal packaging and waste. Even the handkerchief is a nice quality and small, not like grandma’s undies that sometimes come with other scopes. I also dig on the reticle shape which reminds me of an orthodox cross – it’s not too thin or thick, just the way you’d like it (is what she said, yeah, I know…). Also, looking inside the scope with super high lumen light reveals, dare I say, precision – something unexpected at this cost level. I think Sig’s trying to introduce these in the best light possible so as to grab market share. Well, their marketing is your win (for now at least)
But wait, what’s that thing on the side, looks like scribbles or some kind – what IS that?! Meatballs with wafting smell coming off them? Frog eyes? Female crocodile cartoon eyes peeking just above the surface of the water… Let me get closer… Nah, it’s a STAG! With tiny little red beady eyes. And deformed horns. WHO thought of this logo?! Watsamadderwidu?! It’s possible the weirdest logo I’ve ever come across – it’s like slapping flame prints on a Bentley. Iiiish…
But then again, who cars, the paint doesn’t drive the car. So with that little minus, I’d say Sig’s again a winner. BTW, remember the old Nikon Buckmaster scopes? They were totally awesome maaaaaan… But then Nikon got out of the biz, so I’m wondering if there’s any connection between Sig’s Buckmasters and the Nikon Buckmaster series. Whatever the case, I highly recommend this scope. (and if you don’t like the logo, put tape over it!)
text_fidelity_b: Sig Sauer BUCKMASTERS Scope- 3-12x44MM BDC

H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults My wife and I have wanted to get on the water with SUPs or kayaks since trying them on a tour a few years ago, however, unable to have any storage at home, we have been unable to. Then we saw inflatable SUPs and thought we’d be able to give that a try. I had the opportunity to get this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and I jumped! Of course, we live in a hot weather state with summer rainy (storm) season and I’ve had major surgery this year with a longer recovery, so unfortunately we have not yet been able to get onto the water. But as the weather calms and I’ve been cleared... we’ll be out there sooner than later. In the mean time, we finally had a chance to blow up this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board and so far so good - we are sure this is going to turn out to be a great thing for us! This H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board comes with several items to get you going (able cuff, repair kit, pump), but do not forget, you’ll want to have some sort of safety vest (required by law in our state - NOT INCLUDED in this kit).

The pump to get it inflated is included and for us, worked pretty well. We took turns to pump it up and while it took some time (and strength we’re both currently lacking post surgery and injury) we were still able to get it “almost fully inflated.” I say “almost” because the company recommended 15 PSI and we only got to 10. That 15 is for “optimal use” and no higher. We felt like the 10 would be good, but when we are out there (and I have more energy back) we will go a bit higher than the 10 As you can see in the pics, it is very inflated and looks good, my wife able too and on it and feel firm and secure. Standing on it she said it felt like (on water) it’ll have good, solid balance and allow a feeling of security on the water. This SUP looks and feels “narrow and long” to us based on our experiences on tours, but something we both would feel comfortable on. We will update this review once we can get out there. In the mean time, we are really happy with this SUP and how easily it went together. Or blown into shape. The removal of air was easy and took only a couple minutes. I’ll say, when she first opened the valve there was a LOUD HIGH PITCHED!!! sound that hurt both our ears, but it went away pretty quickly. Then completed the air removal. My wife did point out the ONE CON is this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board has a VERY pointy and painful value piece you push on - it was not at all comfortable and hurt her finger enough she grabbed a piece of the wrapping it came in to cushion her finger.

We have not used nor opened the paddle that came with. We felt like its weight in the bag was alright, but had a chance to get another that was lighter. We will try both. But we also feel like having two paddles is safest - one with in case something happens to the second.

There are hooks on the deck where you can attach a kayak seat for sitting down - something I prefer. I have weaker ankles from years of sports, so I can tire easily on SUPs. I’ll look forward to this addition - NOT INCLUDED in this kit, but available from H2O as an add-on.

Overall this H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board is a great board and we are even more excited to get to our coast and use it. In the mean time, we are very happy with how easy this SUP gets set up and takes down and feel like it’s sturdy and well made enough it’ll be great for a good long time.
text_fidelity_b: H2OSUP Inflatable Stand Up Paddle Board 10'6''/10' × 30" × 6" with Premium SUP Paddle Board Accessories & Backpack, Ultra-Light, Wide Stable Design, Non-Slip Deck for Youth & Adults

text_fidelity_a:
Fuliuyu Long Range Green Presentation Pointer High Power Flashlight with USB Cable, Rechargeable Adjustable Focus for Night Astronomy Outdoor Work Pet Interaction Conference While not an indictment of the quality of the product, this laser is listed as being good for interacting with pets. However, this laser is powerful enough to do some serious eye damage! It's powerful enough to pop a dark colored balloon if held in place for a moment. In fact, it's powerful enough that if I point it at the back of my hand and hold it in place for a few seconds, it begins to sting! That's more than bright enough to permanently damage your pet's eyes, especially if you're pointing it towards them in order to get them to chase after it. Lasers like these are not currently well regulated on this site, so you should not assume that they are safe. I'd advise wearing proper laser safety goggles when using this laser, never point it towards a person, and please don't use it to play with your pets!

And now that I've got that diatribe out of the way, the product itself seems fairly well made, and at a decent price. It has a nice protector ring that covers the "on" button to help prevent accidental discharge. This helps with safety, as well as keeping your battery from draining due to accidental use. The beam is pretty well focused, and I don't see much diffusion even 50-100 feet out. On a cloudy day, the laser point (not the beam, but the spot where it is pointed) is clearly visible at 100-200 feet of distance. At night, the beam itself is clearly visible in the atmosphere.
text_fidelity_b: Fuliuyu Long Range Green Presentation Pointer High Power Flashlight with USB Cable, Rechargeable Adjustable Focus for Night Astronomy Outdoor Work Pet Interaction Conference

text_fidelity_a:
Augason Farms Freeze Dried Sweet Corn 16 oz #10 Can Big fan of prepping for emergencies and whatever else that may impact food supplies. I buy from Augason Farms regularly. I have never had any major issues or concerns with any of their products. Sellers yes, products no. I buy emergency food and tuck it away. I try to buy when on sale because I am basically buying food and not eating it. I rarely get into it, or rotate it. If I am buying from Augason farms, then the packaging is just fine for super long term storage (10-25 years depending on the food item). I get the occasional dented can (this one was fine), and it makes no impact. It isnt like other food grade cans where the can is breeched. These cans are made to withstand floods and other crazy stuff. They float, did you know that? Sometimes I will get into a can early if I bought it on sale and it is same price or cheaper than non long term storage equivalent (recently I experienced that with powdered butter. My usual bagged brand was more expensive than the sale price of Augason powdered butter.. stuff like that).

Anyway, I like the corn to be consumed as is, tossed in a big bowl of salad, or rehydrated when used in soups or as a side. Not my number one prep item, but it does add variety.

Occasionally I see people post reviews that say they got an expired product. But they never show a picture of the date they are looking at. The cans show the manufacture date first and foremost, then follows the best by date many many many years in the future. If they got an expired product, then do the math. That means the product would have been made 10-25 years ago. I mean, maybe. Lets see the label. They change the look of their label on occasion. So anyway, I am always suspect of those reviews. I just think they arent reading it right, and if it was legit they would post a pic of the can.
text_fidelity_b: Augason Farms Freeze Dried Sweet Corn 16 oz #10 Can

text_fidelity_a:
EcoZoom Versa, High-Efficiency, Wood-Burning, 14.25 lbs Portable Rocket Stove for Outdoor Cooking First, it must be known that the EcoZoom Versa Camping Stove, in our case today, with our first go isn't as handy as using the kitchen stove. Said stove which still works at this junction is less than 15 feet as the crow flies from the EcoZoom Versa Camping Stove which I set up beside the BBQ grill so as to have a place to set stuff.

We cooked hamburgers, hash brown and pork and beans on the thing awhile ago on a cast iron skillet. Good gracious! I mean a mere piddly handful of twigs cooked the whole meal! It's insane, really. Tell you what...when these things first got popular about 10 years ago I took a look, called it nonsense and never looked back. And then, well, things changed. Our EcoZoom Versa Camping Stove is rightfully the backup for the backup. A real 'just in case' thing. However, were I in it just for fun I could prolly think up a dozen reasons to have one for outdoor fun. But I'm not funning here. I'm very serious. Times are serious.

Not being a metal worker or a brick layer I turned to this device which in all of its simplicity has struck just the right note. It is a little smoky to start, but as it heats up there is very little, just like everyone says. It cooks pretty hot to begin, but by jiggling the sticks we got pretty decent heat control. Smaller sticks for a burst of hot, etc. The next morning I wiped off the outside and spritzed the top and grate with a little spray olive oil as a protectant. I'd estimate that one 5 gal bucket of yard sticks will yield 4-5 complete meals such as I described above.

I'm as pleased as punch, and not a little amazed. What pushed me over was a couple of vids done by EcoZoom Versa Camping Stove's biggest fan in England on YT. In answer to my question he advised that he's had his for over 6 years and uses it regularly. Simple, light weight, and it lasts. If you're circling like I did, go ahead and land on it. You'll be thankin' me. Guaranteed.

Lastly a pro tip. If you are unaccustomed to cooking over wood just be advised to scrub the outside and bottom of your cookware as well as you do the inside. It will get smoky.
text_fidelity_b: EcoZoom Versa, High-Efficiency, Wood-Burning, 14.25 lbs Portable Rocket Stove for Outdoor Cooking

MBB Ab Equipment,Home Ab Machine Function Movement Multiple Core Strength, Abdominal Training 10 in 1 Magic Body Builder with 3 Levels Resistance for Teenage,Women and Men.122 Country Patented I was excited to try this as I love fitness gadgets, and when they added a $10 off coupon, I ordered it even though I read reviews on another brand of the same item from shorter people that it was too big. Turns out for me, they were right. I'm 5' 3", and this is uncomfortable to use to do ab crunches with as it's so long it presses into the top front of my shoulders instead of my upper chest or below, which gets pretty painful after a few reps.

The manufacturer's claim their low resistance level is about 35 pounds of resistance (16kg in pounds) is not true of my unit. I measured the resistance. Moving the smaller side toward the larger only a few inches using a calibrated spring scale, the resistance was 55 pounds - I couldn't move it further as my wrists aren't that strong, but I'd guess it gets to around 75 pounds of resistance when fully compressed.

For upper body moves, over 55 pounds is way too much for someone who isn't already pretty fit. People who have been sedentary, have had injuries or who just aren't that strong could hurt themselves trying to close it or just become frustrated as they wouldn't be able move the two sides together. If you're getting this hoping to start to get fit, it's going to be too strong. At over 55 pounds of resistance if you're under I'd think 5' 8" or taller, the abdominal exercise in the third image is going to hurt - in the picture, the woman has this under her armpit, but think about pushing 60 pounds of pressure with your armpit - ouch! I tried pushing against it with my chest rather than my armpit, but it was too tall. And the padding, which would probably be adequate for resistance of up to 30 pounds, isn't thick enough at over 50 - it presses deeply and slightly painfully into my thighs for adductions.

I do use this for hip adductions - where you put it between your thighs and squeeze. It's pretty challenging, and I am used to doing 100 to 130 pound adductions at the gym, but the ergonomics of the MBB Ab Equipment make most movements more difficult. It shoots out from under me when I try to do some of the floor exercises pictured like what they call "SIDE WAIST" and "WAIST TRAINING"; for the one they call waist training, the Wondercore Smart is better as you can adjust the resistance, it starts out less open, and it's more stable on the floor.

This could be useful to add to your at-home workouts. If you're already pretty strong - not a bodybuilder, but have worked out your chest and arms regularly at over 40 pounds, this unit could be useful. If you haven't, it's going to be very difficult, and I'd recommend you use one of the many thigh master units available here on Amazon, a spring power twister or something like this https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B00OZ0HECI/ with padding on the arms - I use barbell shoulder pads on the arms of mine. It was good for me for hips and inner thighs, but I've been working them regularly for a while now. I wasn't able to use this for everything they claim, but the MBB Ab Equipment is great for hip adductions, okay for chest if I'm careful.
text_fidelity_b: MBB Ab Equipment,Home Ab Machine Function Movement Multiple Core Strength, Abdominal Training 10 in 1 Magic Body Builder with 3 Levels Resistance for Teenage,Women and Men.122 Country Patented

WILD MAN Bike Bag, Bike Accessories, Bike Phone Holder Bike Phone Mount, Waterproof Bike Phone Bag, Mountain Bike Accessories for Adult Bikes with 3D Hard EVA, TPU Touch Screen and Sun Visor for Phones Under 6.7" This is a sort of gem in a way considering I have never heard of the brand. The quality is fantastic to the point where you could easily mistake this for an expensive, established brand. AND...even though Wild Man is or is not a good name, at least it makes sense, more or less, for a bike accessory.

Anyway, it seems like they got everything right, but just be advised that this is NOT the type of case where you can see your phone through the top, despite saying it's compatible with all these devices; that's just a way to add search terms, and I guess it's technically correct that those phones will fit in this bag.

While I haven't had this out in a downpour, it has what appear to be excellent quality, self-sealing zippers on the exterior that should be essentially waterproof as far as rain goes (likely not submersible). It's sort of a "shell" case in that it is semi-rigid, and the material has a checkered carbon fiber look to it, which is neat looking and will likely match a lot of fancier bikes, but will work with anything since it's basically black.

The three straps come large enough that I imagine they can be used with any bike, and can be adjusted down as necessary; I expect the cleanest and nicest installations will involve trimming the excess. The one strap is "across" the opening of the two sections, which would limit how far you can open it, except there is a piece of fabric inside artificially limiting how far you can open it, perhaps so that the former's limitation is not so obvious, but I suspect it will help keep you from dropping stuff out of the case while it is installed on the bike.

One side is a half-height net, and the other side is a full height zippered net, both of which offer some stretch, and are very much like a good piece of luggage.

This definitely adds a little bulk to your bike, and I'm not convinced everyone will want on for permanent storage (there are lots of other placement options to consider), but I can imagine that this goes quite far when doing multi-day riding with camping stops. The great thing is that it can be taken off and put back on quite easily, and as needed.

text_fidelity_a: Razor A4 Kick Scooter OK, so I had to have one of these contraptions.  Both my kids had Zootrs for Eco Challenges and tootling around Chicago but I was going to use mine for exercise.  Good choice since cleaning out a clogged sewer ranks above running and biking on my list of druthers. My initial considerations were finding one for an adult weighing more than 90 pounds and costing less than $300.  This seemed to be about the only one.  Had just purchased a motorized Razor (300) for my daughter to ride back and forth from the train station and was very impressed with its quality. However, the size and weight of my new Razor A4 kick scooter surprised me. It's a trick scooter and one should seriously consider its handlebar warning stating "this object moves when in use. Take safety precautions."  OK, I just turned 65 and I'm probably not in the target demographic group, but I'm getting pretty good on it and look less like an idiot every day.  Caution though because the standing area is short and narrow and I have big feet so I tend to switch legs a lot while using the opposing leg for propulsion.  The wheels are tiny and buck whenever they hit a piece of gravel or a twig.  The "trick" is avoiding obstacles in the street.  Have fun.  It's a good uphill cardio workout, strengthens the quads and glutes and helps get rid of some of those extra butt-cheeks.  I'm going to borrow one of my kids' Zootrs though and save the Razor A4 for exhibition!
text_fidelity_b: Razor A4 Kick Scooter

text_fidelity_a: Gixibata Camping Sleeping Pad, Ultralight Self Inflating Camping Pads with Built-in Pump, Thick 4 inch Lightweight Inflatable Sleeping Mat for Camping, Hiking, Backpacking, Camp Sleep Pad [[VIDEOID:da1735cab448c303be82a6fefb9e543e]] I grabbed this Gixibata Camping Sleeping Pad because my wife and I enjoy days at the beach where we use a tent to have shade in our hot weather, very sunny state. But that sand is brutally hard to lay on - especially on my middle aged back. So I thought this Gixibata Camping Sleeping Pad would help. It comes nicely rolled in an easy to carry bag - it was also easy to refold and get back into the same bag - how often does that happen? The material seems decent. It feels a bit thick - so it’ll hold up against usage, but can’t speak to it’s strength against things poking out of the ground, so I’d still be careful - as one usually should. My wife laid on it - I’m recovering from surgery and still a few weeks out from such things - and said it was decent - she’d be fine on it on the beach as we’re planning. She is the one who pumped it up - video included - and for the most part it’s very easy. Close the stopped on the back of the pillow and leave the one on the pump open, then start pumping. It filled fairly fast - you see almost all of her efforts in the video. Then close the stopper on the pump. This was the only thing we had issue with. For my first time just to test - pad empty - I had a hard time getting it closed. It took me several tries and several minutes before I somehow got it in. My wife had the same issue - I cut the video as she grew frustrated and edited out that frustration. It did FINALLY close, exactly as it had for me - and all was well. So that was weird. Overall we are happy with this Gixibata Camping Sleeping Pad. We do wish closing the stopper was easier, but for now, we deal. In the end we would strongly consider a second one if the need should arise.

SABRE Ruger Tactical Model with Pepper Spray & Practice Spray, Black We have mountain lions and coyote where we live. It's not a bad idea to carry some spray when going on hikes. Especially if you're by yourself.

So this seemed like it might fit the bill. The case seems simple enough, but it had a lot of parts. Parts that could easily get lost. There's a little retainer clip for the thumb trigger that I accidentally popped off with my thumb a few times. There's the cannister retainer clip that is indexed so you can only install it one way. There's a semi clear plug that drops out of the bottom if you decide to switch the belt clip side. So I'd like to see a simplified version of the case.

Loading and unloading is fairly simple. Pull the cannister clip. Lift the trigger clip and thumb trigger and pull out the old cannister and drop in the new one.

Deploying the spray is a simple point at target, insert thumb and press the thumb trigger. The range is not great, but might be enough to make the difference between harm and escape.

I've had some experience CS gas training and had considered trying out some of the spray, but decided against it. Like a fire extinguisher, I'm just going to assume that it works as described.

Also, made in the USA.
text_fidelity_b: SABRE Ruger Tactical Model with Pepper Spray & Practice Spray, Black

The Firm TransFIRMer The FIRM Supercharged Sculpting workout is a highly stylized workout with electronica, artistically designed sets and a clean, sleek mood. This is a combination of traditional weight training with aerobics using the necessary TransFIRMer. Most of the exercises are recognizable as traditional exercises like plank or sit-ups and squats.

The lunges seem easier to do with the TransFIRMer, although weights are used throughout most of the exercises to give them a little more edge. The workout is followed by a brief stretching segment, but if you want to totally relax, there is a "Bonus: 8-minute Stretch Workout."

This set also includes two additional DVDs: The FIRM Ultimate Calorie Blaster and The FIRM Aerobic Body Shaping. If you have any issues with your knees, you may need to try various workouts to see which ones you can manage. I found the Ultimate Calorie Blaster DVD was hard on the knees.

"The TransFIRMer was designed with multiple uses in mind and has 5 different configurations to take each workout to the next level." ~ pg. 6

The TransFIRMer can be positioned in five different ways to increase the possibilities:

6" TransFIRMer - The green section can be used alone
8" TransFIRMer - The blue section can be used alone
14" TransFIRMer - The blue and green sections used together
Side-by-Side TransFIRMer - The blue and green sections placed next to each other
Incline TransFIRMer - The green piece fits into the blue piece for a convenient and stable incline.

"You can adjust the intensity of the workout depending on how high you step." ~ pg. 7

The workout booklet has some interesting rotation calendars so you can plan out 21 days. There is also a section on healthy eating tips, an eating plan, 21-day diet plan, list of 100-calorie snacks and list of 200-calorie snacks. A substitution list makes the diet easier to follow especially if you are eating out and want to still keep to the diet plan.

For years I couldn't do the FIRM workouts because I kept forgetting to buy the equipment, but now with the step at home I can try out most of the new workouts and have fun working out. The 2-piece step is also easy to arrange and is very sturdy. The low-impact exercises work well with the step and the incline is used for push-ups, cardio, arms and ab exercises. If you are buying this step to also use with other workouts that use a step, they say that is not recommended.

~The Rebecca Review
text_fidelity_b: The Firm TransFIRMer

Bulk 120 Piece 4" Glow Stick with Cord Assortment - Ideal For Halloween, New Years, Dances or Emergencies While I was initially very happy to find a pack of 120 glowsticks with strings for a single price, I was less happy to receive the package and discover a grand total of 115 usable glowsticks. There were 2 others that lacked the caps to allow you to tie the strings on, so there were, technically, 117 glowsticks in the package, but I don't regard those two as usable due to the missing caps. There were also 126 strings, though I don't really regard an additional 11 strings as making up for the missing 5 usable glowsticks.

If a company is not going to be packing an accurate amount of product, then they should not advertise by a specific count. I don't have a problem with items packaged by weight so long as that is how they are advertised. This company should have advertised as "3 pounds of glowsticks with strings" or whatever weight it is instead of 120 glowsticks with strings as that is NOT what they delivered. Luckily, I didn't NEED the full 120, but if I had, not getting a bit over 4% of what I paid for would have been even more disappointing.

The quality control for this product does not appear to be very high due to this. I don't yet know how many of these will actually light up, but I'm hoping for all 115 which is why I'm currently giving this 2 stars. If any fail, I'll be reducing the review to 1 stars as I would then have not received more than 5% of what I ordered. Yes, that is a small amount, but I PAID for 120 glowsticks with caps that could be tied with the included strings and NOT 115 glowsticks with caps, 2 without caps, and extra strings.
text_fidelity_b: Bulk 120 Piece 4" Glow Stick with Cord Assortment - Ideal For Halloween, New Years, Dances or Emergencies

Snell MTB Black Golf Balls I've used both the red and black now. I would have to say the red is better for hard, Florida style, courses. I used them in Florida this winter and was very impressed. The black is better for the northern (midwest) style courses. I've played on the soft early spring in Ohio and liked the black better. Without getting in to the technology (plenty of that available from the experts), let's just say I found the red held the greens better, but lacked a little ball flight. The black held soft greens very well and seemed to have more flight distance. As the summer heat dries out the local courses I'll switch back to the red, but early season the black is the better choice.

Bottom line, I suggest buying both red and black and use the better of the two depending on the course conditions.

Both are soft, bounce off the club face, hold the line, but can be worked (fade of draw) as well as any ball I've played. I'm a 10-12 handicapper so I'm not a "pro", but I'm planning to buy more later in the season. I'm very happy with them!
text_fidelity_b: Snell MTB Black Golf Balls
